Add 9 · Level 1.heading: Hear the added note. Name the chord.
Add 9 · Level 1.intro: You will hear a three-note chord with one extra note added. Choose the add 9 chord type that matches the sound.

steps.title: Listen to the whole chord
steps.description: Press Play to hear the four notes together. Listen to the sound they make as a group. You can listen again whenever you need to.

steps.title: Choose the chord type
steps.description: Select Major add 9, Minor add 9, Diminished add 9 or Augmented add 9. The extra note is present in every answer, so listen for the type of chord underneath it.

steps.title: Submit your answer
steps.description: When you are ready, press Submit Answer. You can change your choice before you submit.

Add 9 · Level 1.about: An add 9 chord starts with a triad, a chord made of three notes, and adds one more note called the ninth. For example, F major uses F, A and C. Adding G makes F major add 9. That extra note can sit between the other notes, so it does not have to be the highest sound. This lesson uses chords built on F. The notes are kept in a close layout. The chords use one arrangement throughout this lesson. Choose only the chord type; there is no separate inversion answer.
Add 9 · Level 1.layoutCaption: F major add 9: F, A and C, with G added between F and A.
Add 9 · Level 1.exampleExplanation: This visual example shows F major with an added G. Choose Major add 9. In the quiz, choose the chord type you hear, even when the notes are arranged differently.
